messages.subject: Reorder plots in facet_grid
parts:
Hi,
Here is my dataset:http://dl.dropbox.com/u/1852742/wntpathwaydata.csv

I am making a facetted figure that plots the expressions by gene:
#Wnt Pathway Plot Code

setwd('C:/Documents and Settings/jjm688/Desktop/Rdata')
re=read.csv('wntpathwaydata.csv')
wntpath=re[c(1:18,28:36,64:72,82:90),]
p=ggplot(wntpath,aes(tp,relexp))+geom_point()+geom_line()+
facet_grid(gene~.)+
geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=relexp-se,ymax=relexp+se),width=.1)
p+scale_x_continuous('Time (Hours)')+
scale_y_continuous('Relative Expression')

It is ordering the genes by alphabet but I want to order them as
Wnt2b, Wnt3, Wnt5a, Myc, and Sfrp1.

I started learning ggplot2 back in November but haven't used it
since. I assume that the solution will involve factor levels but I
can't remember how to use that. Thanks for your help!

Jahan

On 6/9/2011 7:37 AM, Jahan wrote:
> Hi,
> Here is my dataset:http://dl.dropbox.com/u/1852742/wntpathwaydata.csv
>
> I am making a facetted figure that plots the expressions by gene:
> #Wnt Pathway Plot Code
>
> setwd('C:/Documents and Settings/jjm688/Desktop/Rdata')
> re=read.csv('wntpathwaydata.csv')
> wntpath=re[c(1:18,28:36,64:72,82:90),]
> p=ggplot(wntpath,aes(tp,relexp))+geom_point()+geom_line()+
> facet_grid(gene~.)+
> geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=relexp-se,ymax=relexp+se),width=.1)
> p+scale_x_continuous('Time (Hours)')+
> scale_y_continuous('Relative Expression')
>
> It is ordering the genes by alphabet but I want to order them as
> Wnt2b, Wnt3, Wnt5a, Myc, and Sfrp1.
>
> I started learning ggplot2 back in November but haven't used it
> since. I assume that the solution will involve factor levels but I
> can't remember how to use that. Thanks for your help!
>
> Jahan

# Since you made the data available at at URL, you can use it directly
re=read.csv('http://dl.dropbox.com/u/1852742/wntpathwaydata.csv')

# Definition of the genes you want and the order you want them in
genes <- c("Wnt 2b", "Wnt 3", "Wnt 5a", "Myc", "Sfrp 1")
# Different way to select the desired subset of data, but more
# descriptive and less subject to breakage if something changes
# about the underlying data.
wntpath <- re[re[["gene"]] %in% genes,]
# Change the order of the levels of the factor to control the order of
# plotting the facets (default is alphabetic)
wntpath[["gene"]] <- factor(wntpath[["gene"]], levels=genes)

# this ggplot call is equalivant to yours; I reflexively reformatted
# it to my personal style to make sure I understood it.
ggplot(wntpath,aes(tp,relexp)) +
geom_point() +
geom_line() +
geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=relexp-se,ymax=relexp+se),width=.1) +
facet_grid(gene~.) +
